newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin appears on TV, said to be recovering well.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin appears on TV, said to be recovering well.

text.p: Boris Yeltsin appeared on Russian television on Tuesday for the first time in three weeks and his spokesman, responding to concern about his health, said the president was staging a steady recovery from pneumonia.
Looking alert and smiling, Yeltsin was shown shaking hands and chatting with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin during a short working trip to the Kremlin.
But the long-awaited television appearance and the official reassurances seemed unlikely to quell speculation about the president's long-term health and ability to rule Russia.
"My personal impression of the president today is that progress is evident," Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky told reporters.
"I think the president will gradually be increasing his physical activity and his workload," Yastrzhembsky said, adding that Yeltsin was likely to hold more meetings this week.

During his three-hour Kremlin trip Yeltsin discussed a range of issues with Chernomyrdin, including Monday's elections in breakaway Chechnya and a planned visit to Moscow by French President Jacques Chirac at the weekend.

Asked about the view of doctors on Yeltsin's visit to the Kremlin, Yastrzhembsky said jokingly: "Either the president overcame the resistance of his doctors or, more likely, they considered his condition had improved somewhat."

Yeltsin, who spent months away from the Kremlin last year because of health problems and underwent heart surgery on November 5, is often described by aides and doctors as a restless patient who resents having to cut his workload.

Until Tuesday, Yeltsin had not been seen on television or in public since he fell ill with double pneumonia on January 6 -- a gap even longer than the two-week disappearance from public view after his heart bypass operation.

There was, unusually for Russia, no television footage of his last visit to the Kremlin, which aides said took place last Wednesday as the State Duma lower house of parliament debated a move to force him to quit.
Despite Yastrzhembsky's upbeat tone on Tuesday, Russian newspapers said rumours about the president's health would not go away.

"A new wave of infernal rumours about the health of the president is inevitable, and they are becoming harder to refute," Sevodnya said in a front-page story which suggested that Yeltsin could be ill with some "third disease".
Sovietskaya Rossiya, one of the leading anti-government newspapers, published a cartoon showing a glowering president apparently steering the ship of state from his hospital bed.

The communist opposition is behind the moves in the Duma to oust him on health grounds, although it acknowledges that the legal justification is shaky, given a constitution that grants the president strong powers.
Yeltsin's rivals, including former security chief Alexander Lebed, are jockeying for position in case of an early vote.
Lebed told Reuters on Tuesday he was sure a presidential election would be held soon. "I am getting ready," he said.
Yastrzhembsky also sounded a note of caution over the president's health.
"The president has not fully recovered after his double pneumonia. This is an illness that demands a prolonged period of recovery," said Yastrzhembsky.
"This is why he must refrain from flying," the spokesman added, referring to Yeltsin's decision on Monday to call off a planned trip to the Netherlands at short notice.
Yastrzhembsky said Yeltsin would spend his 66th birthday on Saturday with his family.
